title: Contracted GPU credit multipliers and deferred burst log — Dec 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines the "contract credit multiplier" model and a deferred-burst ledger we use to honor short-term demand spikes for Dedicated customers while preserving long-term fairness. Goal: encode multiplier tiers, decay windows, cross-region penalties, and an audit-friendly per-contract log for Q1 2027 capacity planning.

Summary of concepts:
- Baseline allocation: guaranteed capacity (GPUs and baseline hours/mo) from contract.
- Multiplier tiers: extra burst credits = baseline * (multiplier - 1). Applied when pool utilization < 95% but per-contract consumption > baseline.
- Deferred burst: unused burst credits can be carried forward into a limited window and consumed later (subject to decay).
- Cross-region penalty: consuming burst from another region uses a penalty factor (0.6 multiplier on availability) and increments egress accounting.
- Contention policy: when pool is saturated, scoring = (commitment_weight * 0.6) + (multiplier_weight * 0.3) + (tenure_bonus * 0.1).

Ledger (example rows — columns are commaseparated for portability):
ContractID,Customer,Region,Committed_GPUs,Baseline_Hrs_per_GPU_per_month,Multiplier_Tier,Monthly_Burst_Credits_hrs,Deferred_Burst_on_hand_hrs,Decay_window_days,CrossRegionPenalty,Notes
CR-2107,FernLabs,us-west1,40,720,1.25,7200,1200,30,0.6,Large seasonal spikes; allow 2x monthly burst in Nov-Dec
CR-1998,AtlasHealth,eu-west2,16,720,1.5,5760,0,14,0.6,Strict SLA; burst usage restricted to <30% of peak traffic
CR-2372,NeptuneAI,us-east1,8,720,1.1,576,200,60,0.7,Deferred credits from Q4 promo; prefer local pooling
CR-2411,Snowcap,ap-southeast1,24,720,1.4,3456,600,45,0.5,Multi-region failover enabled; cross-region allowed with cost recovery

Sample calculation (CR-2107):
- Baseline monthly hours = Committed_GPUs * Baseline_Hrs_per_GPU_per_month = 40 * 720 = 28,800 hrs
- Multiplier 1.25 => Monthly burst capacity = baseline * (multiplier - 1) = 28,800 * 0.25 = 7,200 hrs
- If they used 30,000 hrs in a month => overage 1,200 hrs. 1,200 hrs drawn from burst pool leaving 6,000 hrs. Overage beyond burst billed via overage slug.

Deferred burst rules:
- Credits that went unused in a month can be carried forward up to Deferred_Burst_on_hand_hrs cap.
- Decay schedule: each carried hour ages linearly and decays by 1/Decay_window_days of its remaining value per day (approx exponential decay target) to prevent indefinite accumulation.
- Expiration: credits older than 90 days automatically expire.

Allocation algorithm (for operations and planner):
1) At allocation tick (1 minute): evaluate regional pool utilization.
2) If util < 95% and customer demand > baseline, allow draw from their monthly burst bucket up to available_burst * min(1, pool_headroom/burst_demand).
3) If customer has deferred credits, burn deferred credits first (they have smaller internal cost) but respect decay and per-contract caps.
4) If pool is saturated, run contention scoring; in ties, prefer the contract with higher tenure then higher multiplier tier.
5) Cross-region draws apply CrossRegionPenalty: available_burst_effective = burst_hrs * CrossRegionPenalty. Billing and accounting log both raw and effective consumption.

Operational knobs (to tune in console):
- pool_headroom_threshold (default 0.05)
- per_contract_max_burst_fraction (default 0.5)
- deferred_decay_days (default 30)
- cross_region_penalty_map (per-region pair overrides)

Open questions / edge cases (notes to infra/product):
- How to reflect burst consumption to customer-facing SLA dashboards (same as tokens/day or separate burst_histogram?)
- Billing cadence for deferred credits consumed after month boundary (apply to next invoice or prorate?)
- Admin override path for emergency bursts (manual approvals with TTL).

Audit sample (recent events log excerpt):
2026-11-21,CR-2107,draw,us-west1,150hrs,source=monthly_burst
2026-11-24,CR-2372,draw-cross-region,us-east1->us-west1,40hrs,penalty=0.7,charged=28hrs_effective
2026-12-03,CR-1998,carry-forward,eu-west2,200hrs,from=Nov

Decision points for Q1 2027 planning:
- Default multiplier tiers recommended: 1.1, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0. Map to contract sizes: small (<10 GPUs)=1.1, mid=1.25, large>=40=1.5, enterprise negotiations up to 2.0.
- Enable 14-day deferred carry for regulated customers; others get 30 days.
- Implement a chargeback metric: "effective_gpu_hours" to reflect cross-region penalty for internal cost dashboards.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Miguel to prototype decay curve as a lambda and run simulation against Nov traffic (due 2026-12-20).
- Rina to add UI mockups for Console "Burst Ledger" and per-contract history (due 2026-12-22).
- Jonah to update billing export to include deferred credit flags and effective hours (JIRA-INFRA-889) (due 2027-01-05).

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally conservative on deferred carry windows to avoid long-term capacity pollution. We should run a Monte Carlo on region-seasonal spikes before finalizing multipliers.

Appendix: quick glossary
- baseline: guaranteed allocation computed as GPUs * baseline_hours
- burst credits: extra hours available in month before overage billing
- deferred: carried burst hours across months subject to caps/decay
- cross-region penalty: factor applied when bursting outside contracted region

End of doc.
